target_customer: Mobile, web and IoT developers who wanted a managed GraphQL backend
problem: Developers wanted GraphQL backends without building servers. Scaphold offered GraphQL as a service with push notifications, analytics, file storage and custom code.
business_model: Developer platform subscription (freemium backend as a service)

founders.name: Michael Paris
founders.background_notes: YC page says he began at Microsoft working on databases and, after Scaphold was sold to AWS, built AWS AppSync there.

competitors.name: Firebase
competitors.what: Google's mobile and web backend as a service
competitors.traction_then: Developers in 2017 judged it ahead of GraphQL BaaS on features

technical_complexity.rationale: Generating a GraphQL API from a schema plus hosted auth, files and push is standard backend work with the GraphQL spec still young in 2016.

defensibility.rationale: Open GraphQL tooling and larger BaaS players meant features were copyable; lock-in was minimal.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: AWS absorbed the company, and its founder built AWS AppSync, a managed GraphQL service (date not found).

market_need_then: GraphQL was gaining developer attention in 2016 and 2017 but few hosted options existed; Scaphold reached Product Hunt with endorsements from YC partners.

branding.domain_note: scaphold.io now redirects to an unrelated third party domain.

brand_strength.rationale: The name suggests scaffolding for backends, but it is a misspelling and sources show no mascot, community or brand press.

outcome_analysis: Scaphold was a two person GraphQL backend as a service startup from YC W17 that raised only the standard YC amount per aggregators. The YC page says it was sold to AWS and its CEO went on to build AWS AppSync, which points to a team and technology absorption rather than a standalone business. The date and price are not public.
notes: Acquisition date, price and AWS announcement not found; source is the YC company page. CB Insights shows $120K seed from Y Combinator (March 2017) but also a $20.5M total elsewhere; neither is verified so no round is recorded. The scaphold.io site redirects to an unrelated domain and was not followed. Only one dated competitor source was found. Founder education not found. A search summary conflicted with the YC page on whether Paris or Ning built AppSync; the YC page text opened directly was used. Completeness pass: the $120K seed from Y Combinator (March 2017) rests on a single database, CB Insights. The $20.5M total mentioned earlier remains unverified and unexplained. Cross-check search found no independent source for the round or for the AWS acquisition beyond the YC page.
